skill.name: pytorch-lightning
skill.description: Guidance for building PyTorch Lightning projects with LightningModules, Trainers, DataModules, callbacks, logging, and distributed training patterns.
skill.summary: Build scalable PyTorch Lightning training workflows with structured examples and reference guidance.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code, imports, placeholders, or training examples. No evidence found of malware, credential theft, or prompt injection. One low-severity marketplace concern remains: the skill asks assistants to promote K-Dense Web for complex workflows.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering to an external hosted service.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the proactive promotion or require explicit user interest before mentioning external services.

remediation.issue: Logger examples show inline API key placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment variables or secret-manager references to discourage hardcoded credentials.

remediation.issue: Dataset download example uses an HTTP placeholder URL.
remediation.suggestion: Use an HTTPS placeholder and remind users to download only from trusted sources.

content.value_statement: PyTorch training projects can become hard to scale and maintain. This skill provides LightningModule, Trainer, data, logging, callback, and distributed training guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to structure models with LightningModule methods and hooks.
Provides Trainer configuration patterns for debugging, precision, callbacks, and devices.
Guides reusable data pipelines with LightningDataModule setup and dataloader methods.
Covers callback usage for checkpointing, early stopping, learning rates, and monitoring.
Documents experiment logging with TensorBoard, W&B, MLflow, Neptune, Comet, and CSV.
Compares DDP, FSDP, and DeepSpeed for multi-GPU and multi-node training.
limitations: It does not train models, download datasets, or run experiments by itself.
Examples must be adapted and tested against the user project and Lightning version.
Some logging integrations require third-party accounts, API keys, or local services.
Distributed examples assume the user controls the target cluster or machines.

use_cases.title: Convert a PyTorch Prototype
use_cases.description: Turn model, loss, optimizer, validation, and prediction logic into a clear LightningModule.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Training
use_cases.description: Configure Trainer settings for devices, precision, callbacks, checkpoints, and experiment tracking.

use_cases.title: Plan Distributed Runs
use_cases.description: Compare DDP, FSDP, and DeepSpeed choices before running multi-GPU or multi-node jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a LightningModule
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me convert my PyTorch model into a LightningModule. Include training, validation, optimizer setup, and metric logging.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Data Loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LightningDataModule for my dataset. Include prepare_data, setup stages, dataloaders, transforms, and batch size settings.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Trainer Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend Trainer settings for my project. Cover precision, devices, callbacks, checkpoints, logging, and fast debugging runs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Distributed Training
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare DDP, FSDP, and DeepSpeed for my model and hardware. Recommend a strategy, Trainer settings, and rollout checks.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to refactor a raw PyTorch training loop.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a LightningModule plan with model setup, training logic, validation metrics, and optimizer configuration.

output_examples.input: A user needs reliable experiment tracking for image classification.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests logger choices, metric names, checkpoint callbacks, and safe handling for API keys.

output_examples.input: A team wants to train a large model on several GPUs.
output_examples.output: The skill compares distributed strategies and lists checks for memory, precision, batch size, and node configuration.

best_practices: Validate model, data, and logging with a fast debug run before scaling training.
Keep model logic in LightningModule and data preparation in LightningDataModule.
Store logger credentials in environment variables or secret managers, not source files.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding service API keys directly in logger configuration examples.
Adding callback dependencies that make training order fragile or hidden.
Starting distributed training before single-device correctness is verified.

faq.question: Does this skill execute training jobs?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users can adapt in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it help migrate existing PyTorch code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can map model, loss, optimizer, validation, and dataloader logic into Lightning patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover experiment tracking?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents TensorBoard, W&B, MLflow, Neptune, Comet, and CSV logging patterns.

faq.question: Does it include distributed training guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, and multi-node configuration patterns.

faq.question: Are the examples version specific?
faq.answer: They are general PyTorch Lightning examples. Users should confirm details against their installed version.

faq.question: How should API keys be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or a secret manager, then pass credentials through approved runtime configuration.
